newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian guard blasts own men over hospital attack.
newsitem.headline: Albanian guard blasts own men over hospital attack.

text.p: Albania's Republican Guard on Monday condemned a shooting attack by members of one of its units on a military hospital in Tirana and vowed to prevent such incidents in the future.
"The incident by a group of guardsmen over the military hospital...is completely unacceptable," the guard command said in a statement read on state-run television.

"The command expresses its regrets to the hospital staff and wants to assure it that such acts will never occur in the future." It did not say whether those involved in Sunday's attack had been identified and would be punished.

Some 500 hospital workers demonstrated for two hours in protest against what they called an "unprecedented violation" of the prominent hospital where hundreds of people in the quasi-anarchic Balkan country are treated every day.

"Hands off the white uniforms, we are here for saving people," they cried out, while trade union leader Margarita Minai told reporters they would quit if authorities failed to stop violence and protect them.
The attack on the hospital underscored the lawlessness gripping Albania since March when thousands of people rioted over the loss of their savings in dubious pyramid investment schemes.

Hospital sources said some 50 to 60 guardsmen, dressed in civilian clothing, had stormed the hospital to avenge the death of a fellow guardsman who died of wounds there following a shootout on Friday in the central town of Cerrik.
"All the hospital staff tried to save him, but it was not possible," director Ismail Kajo said.

He said the guardsmen, driving two vans with official licence plates and two armoured personnel carriers, opened fire on the hospital on Sunday morning before beating up his deputy and disarming military police charged with hospital security.
The fusillade left bullet holes in the hospital's facade, although no shooting injuries were reported. Staff and patients were scared and refused to respond to reporters' questions.
"We ordered our police not to open fire, just to avoid bloodshed, but we will not tolerate any more such banditry," Defence Minister Shaqir Vukaj said after visiting the hospital.
Vukaj said Prime Minister Bashkim Fino had called an urgent cabinet meeting before leaving for Italy and ordered leading institutions and officials to investigate the matter.
In a statement, the Council of Ministers said it viewed the event "as extremely grave and with unforeseen consequences".

"After hearing a report from the Commander of the Guard of the Republic, Prime Minister Bashkim Fino asked leading officials of the state's main institutions to publicly denounce this unprecedented incident," it said.
"The cabinet members expressed indignation and condemned Sunday's incident at the military hospital, considering it an unworthy and dangerous act for the Guard of the Republic."
It said the government had demanded prosecution and punishment for the organisers "of this grave, shameful and dangerous event for Albanian democracy".

The Interior Ministry originally said five policemen were killed in Cerrik in a gunfight with an armed gang that had occupied a police station. But medical sources said the wounded brought to the hospital from Cerrik were actually guardsmen.
Many parts of Albania are still lawless after the violent unrest of February and March that saw looting and rioting break out across the poverty-stricken formerly communist country.
